description: Unified Rust framework for building, verifying, and testing web apps. Kernel-based architecture for Lean 4 verification and GPU acceleration. Built-in red-teaming tools for automated vulnerability detection.

written.description: Gives an agent a browser that controls its own network traffic, so the model can capture, edit, replay and compare the requests a web app sends without a proxy in between. Each session runs under a network policy and records every fetch it allowed or refused.

alive.last_commit_message:
websec/browser: nudge toward `--as` when a replay goes out unauthenti… (#745)

* websec/browser: nudge toward `--as` when a replay goes out unauthenticated

Since the proxy-focused rewrite, `resend`/`replay` send a stored request's own
bytes and do not pull from the session cookie jar — the jar is opt-in via `--as`.
A common confusion follows: you log in (the browser's Set-Cookie lands in the
jar), then replay a request captured before that login and it goes out with no
Cookie, silently unauthenticated, with nothing saying why.

Detect that case and surface a one-line note pointing at `--as`. In
`edit_then_send` (the one path both replay verbs reach), when the send does not
use the jar, carries no Cookie of its own, and the jar *does* hold cookies for
the target origin (`Jar::header_for`, the HTTP view — not `document_cookie`,
which omits HttpOnly), attach a `hint` to the `Edited` outcome. It rides the
resend envelope and `h5i browser resend` prints it to stderr (so `h5i websec
replay`, which inherits that stderr, shows it once; stdout — the response the
caller greps — is untouched). No hint when the caller set a Cookie themselves
(a forged token is deliberate) or passed `--as`.

Also document the jar/`--as` rule in the websec skill (a fifth "easier to know
than to discover" note on replay).

* test: deflake a_browser_that_fails_is_reported_and_exits_non_zero

The test rewrote the agent-browser stub to fail, but the crude replacement
(`echo boom; exit 3` for everything but `--version`) also failed the
`session list` / probe calls the CLI and session daemon make around a verb.
Under load those sometimes resolved first, so the CLI reported the probe's
failure rather than the click's, and stderr lacked "boom" (~1 in 8 in the full
parallel suite; 0/40 in isolation — a parallelism/timing flake, not a product
bug). This was introduced with the proxy-focused browser model (#744) and is
unrelated to the replay-cookie hint on this branch.

Make the failing stub answer `--version` and `session list` like the real one
and fail only the actual verb, so only the click produces "boom". 0/25 under
added load after the change. Also widen the assertion message to print the
status/stderr/stdout on failure.
